article.howTitle: How to convert CHM to PDF
article.chooseStep: Choose or drop a .chm file. The converter opens the help topics and prepares a preview.
article.waitStep: Review the preview. Large manuals may take longer to open.
article.saveStep: Select Save as PDF, then choose Save as PDF as the destination in your browser’s print dialog. Save the file to read, share, or print later.
article.what: CHM stands for Compiled HTML Help, a Microsoft format that packages HTML topics, images, and a table of contents into one file. It is common in older Windows help files, software manuals, and some ebooks. PDF is easier to open across devices and keeps a fixed layout for printing.
article.layout: The converter puts the help topics in one document, following the table of contents when available. It preserves selectable, searchable text, basic formatting, code, and supported embedded images. Topics are reflowed for printing, so styling and pagination can differ from the original. The default paper size is A4.
article.privacy: The conversion runs entirely in your browser. Your CHM and PDF stay on your device, and remote resources in the help file are not loaded.
